title: Angel Falls
summary: Angel Falls, Salto Angel, drops from Auyan-tepui in Canaima National Park in Venezuela and is given as 979 m high by a Venezuelan tourism site. UNESCO says Canaima holds the world's highest waterfall. The tourism page says aviator Jimmy Angel first mentioned it in his flight log in 1933.

uncertainty.note: Year of Jimmy Angel's first flight-log mention; the page says the falls were already known beyond the Pemon before 1933.

as_recorded.value: in 1933 Angel first mentions seeing the

where.modern_name: Angel Falls (Salto Angel), Auyan-tepui, Canaima National Park, Bolívar State, Venezuela

importance.justification: Often cited as the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, in a UNESCO-listed park.

reviewer_note: Weakest of the batch: the 979 m height and the 1933 date come from a tourism page (class other); UNESCO's English text says only that the park has the world's highest waterfall (1,000 m). Pin is Wikidata only; UNESCO's property point (5 20 N, 62 2 W) is the park centre, not the falls. The date is the 1933 sighting, not a geological age.
